description.value: This study examined behavioral and neural correlates of compulsive alcohol seeking in heavy and light drinkers using a reward incentive delay task with aversive electric-shock threats during fMRI.

spans.text: This study assessed the neural correlates of compulsive alcohol seeking in HDs.

value: We hypothesized that heavy drinkers would seek alcohol points despite the threat of aversive consequences to a higher degree than light drinkers.
We further hypothesized that compulsive alcohol seeking would be associated with a neural circuit involving the mPFC, the insula, and the dorsal and ventral striatum.

spans.text: We hypothesized that heavy drinkers would seek alcohol points despite the threat of aversive consequences to a higher degree than light drinkers.

description.value: Cross-sectional, non-treatment-seeking heavy and light drinkers completed an fMRI task; participants were not randomized or assigned to intervention arms.

spans.text: Finally, our study was cross-sectional, limiting causal interpretations.
